Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verse 4:

﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾ meaning, in repelling the signs of Allah through denial and rejection, ﴿except those who disbelieved﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two verses, none more severe for those who dispute about the Qur'an: 'None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieved' and 'Indeed, those who differ concerning the Scripture are in extreme dissension'" [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/292.]] [al-Baqarah: 176].

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad informed us, Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn Humayd informed us, al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Layth, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed, disputing about the Qur'an is disbelief" [[al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/273 to 'Abd ibn Humayd, and there is weakness in Layth. See also: al-Kafi al-Shafi p. (144). It was narrated by al-Tayalisi in al-Musnad p. 302 and al-Bayhaqi from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr with the wording: "Do not dispute about the Qur'an, for disputing about it is disbelief." See: al-Fath al-Samawi: 3/975-976; Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/615.]].

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran informed us, Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a people disputing about the Qur'an, so he said: "Those before you were destroyed only because of this: they struck the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, some of it against others. The Book of Allah was revealed so that some of it confirms others, so do not deny some of it by means of others. What you know of it, say it; and what you do not know of it, leave it to its knower" [[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (Kitab al-Jami' of Imam Ma'mar): 11/217; Imam Ahmad: 2/195; and Ibn Majah with similar meaning, no. (85) in the Introduction: 1/33, and he said in al-Zawa'id: its chain is sound and its narrators are trustworthy. It was attributed in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/171 to al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and in it is Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar.]].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾, meaning their going about the lands for trade and their safety therein despite their disbelief, for indeed the outcome of their affair is punishment. Its parallel is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "Let not the movement of those who disbelieved throughout the land deceive you" [Al 'Imran: 196].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verses 5–7:

﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and the factions after them.﴾ They are the disbelievers who formed factions (tahazzabu) against their prophets with denial after the people of Noah. ﴿Every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: to kill him and destroy him. It was also said: to take him captive. The Arabs call a captive "akhidh" (one seized). ﴿And they disputed with falsehood to refute﴾ i.e., to nullify, ﴿thereby the truth﴾ which the messengers brought. Their disputation was like their saying: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾ [Ibrahim: 10], and "Why have angels not been sent down to us?" [al-Furqan: 21], and similar things. ﴿So I seized them, and how was My punishment?﴾

﴿Thus the word of your Lord has come into effect﴾ meaning: just as the word of punishment came into effect upon the denying nations, ﴿against those who disbelieved﴾ among your people, ﴿that they are the companions of the Fire.﴾ Al-Akhfash said: "because they are" or "that they are the companions of the Fire."

﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believed: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire."﴾ (7)

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it﴾: the bearers of the Throne and those who circle it, and they are the Karubiyyun (cherubim), who are the chiefs of the angels. Ibn 'Abbas said: the distance between the bearers of the Throne from the ankle of one of them to the bottom of his feet is a journey of five hundred years. [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat: 2/143; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/275–276 attributed it to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh.] It is related that their feet are in the depths of the earths, and the earths and heavens reach to their waists, and they say: "Glory be to the Possessor of might and majesty, glory be to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty, glory be to the Living who does not die; Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit."

Maysara ibn 'Aruba said: their feet are in the lowest earth, and their heads have pierced the Throne; they are in humble submission, not raising their gaze, and they are more fearful than the people of the seventh heaven, and the people of the seventh heaven are more fearful than the people of the heaven next to them, and the next is more fearful than the one after it. Mujahid said: between the angels and the Throne are seventy veils of light.

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been permitted to speak of an angel of Allah's angels, of the bearers of the Throne, that the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah, chapter on the Jahmiyya: 7/17, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat: 2/142 with a sound chain; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/274 attributed it also to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, and Ibn Mardawayh.]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: [Indeed] between one leg of the legs of the Throne and the second leg is the fluttering of a swift bird for thirty thousand years, and the Throne is clothed every day in seventy thousand colours of light, and no creature of Allah's creation can look at it, and all things in the Throne are like a ring in a desert.

Mujahid said: between the seventh heaven and the Throne are seventy thousand veils of light, and a veil of darkness, a veil of light and a veil of darkness.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Around the Throne are seventy thousand rows of angels, row behind row, circling the Throne; these come forward and those turn back, and when some of them meet others, these say "La ilaha illa Allah" and those say "Allahu akbar." Behind them are seventy thousand rows standing, their hands to their necks, placed upon their shoulders; when they hear the takbir and tahlil of those, they raise their voices, saying: "Glory be to You and praise, how great You are and how exalted; You are Allah, there is no god but You, You are the Greatest; all creation will return to You." Behind these are a hundred thousand rows of angels who have placed the right hand upon the left; none of them is glorifying with a praise that another does not glorify with; the distance between the two wings of one of them is a journey of three hundred years, and between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is four hundred years. Allah has veiled Himself from the angels around the Throne with seventy veils of fire, seventy veils of darkness, seventy veils of light, seventy veils of white pearl, seventy veils of red ruby, [seventy veils of yellow ruby,] seventy veils of green emerald, seventy veils of snow, seventy veils of water, seventy veils of hail, and what none knows but Allah the Exalted. He said: Each of the bearers of the Throne and those around it has four faces: the face of an ox, the face of a lion, the face of an eagle, and the face of a human; and each of them has four wings: two wings over his face lest he look at the Throne and be struck senseless, and two wings with which he flies; they have no speech except glorification, praise, magnification and exaltation. [See: Zad al-Masir: 7/208.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿They glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him﴾: they affirm that He is One, with no partner.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani narrated to us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, Umar ibn Abd Allah al-Raqqashi narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Harun ibn Rabab narrated to us, Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, who said: The bearers of the Throne are eight; four of them say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; praise be to You for Your forbearance after Your knowledge," and four of them say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; praise be to You for Your pardon after Your power." He said: And it is as though they are looking at the sins of the children of Adam. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir: 4/73.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And ask forgiveness for those who believed﴾, meaning they say: "Our Lord." ﴿You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾: it was said that it is in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir), and it was said it is by transposition (naql), meaning: Your mercy and Your knowledge have encompassed all things. ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾, that is, Your religion, ﴿and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire.﴾ Mutarrif said: The most sincere of Allah's servants toward the believers are the angels, and the most deceitful of creation toward the believers are the devils. [See: al-Qurtubi 15/295.]

﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believed: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire."﴾ (7)

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it﴾: the bearers of the Throne and those who circle it, and they are the Karubiyyun (cherubim), who are the chiefs of the angels. Ibn 'Abbas said: the distance between the bearers of the Throne from the ankle of one of them to the bottom of his feet is a journey of five hundred years. [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat: 2/143; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/275–276 attributed it to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh.] It is related that their feet are in the depths of the earths, and the earths and heavens reach to their waists, and they say: "Glory be to the Possessor of might and majesty, glory be to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty, glory be to the Living who does not die; Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit."

Maysara ibn 'Aruba said: their feet are in the lowest earth, and their heads have pierced the Throne; they are in humble submission, not raising their gaze, and they are more fearful than the people of the seventh heaven, and the people of the seventh heaven are more fearful than the people of the heaven next to them, and the next is more fearful than the one after it. Mujahid said: between the angels and the Throne are seventy veils of light.

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been permitted to speak of an angel of Allah's angels, of the bearers of the Throne, that the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah, chapter on the Jahmiyya: 7/17, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat: 2/142 with a sound chain; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/274 attributed it also to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, and Ibn Mardawayh.]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: [Indeed] between one leg of the legs of the Throne and the second leg is the fluttering of a swift bird for thirty thousand years, and the Throne is clothed every day in seventy thousand colours of light, and no creature of Allah's creation can look at it, and all things in the Throne are like a ring in a desert.

Mujahid said: between the seventh heaven and the Throne are seventy thousand veils of light, and a veil of darkness, a veil of light and a veil of darkness.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Around the Throne are seventy thousand rows of angels, row behind row, circling the Throne; these come forward and those turn back, and when some of them meet others, these say "La ilaha illa Allah" and those say "Allahu akbar." Behind them are seventy thousand rows standing, their hands to their necks, placed upon their shoulders; when they hear the takbir and tahlil of those, they raise their voices, saying: "Glory be to You and praise, how great You are and how exalted; You are Allah, there is no god but You, You are the Greatest; all creation will return to You." Behind these are a hundred thousand rows of angels who have placed the right hand upon the left; none of them is glorifying with a praise that another does not glorify with; the distance between the two wings of one of them is a journey of three hundred years, and between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is four hundred years. Allah has veiled Himself from the angels around the Throne with seventy veils of fire, seventy veils of darkness, seventy veils of light, seventy veils of white pearl, seventy veils of red ruby, [seventy veils of yellow ruby,] seventy veils of green emerald, seventy veils of snow, seventy veils of water, seventy veils of hail, and what none knows but Allah the Exalted. He said: Each of the bearers of the Throne and those around it has four faces: the face of an ox, the face of a lion, the face of an eagle, and the face of a human; and each of them has four wings: two wings over his face lest he look at the Throne and be struck senseless, and two wings with which he flies; they have no speech except glorification, praise, magnification and exaltation. [See: Zad al-Masir: 7/208.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿They glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him﴾: they affirm that He is One, with no partner.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani narrated to us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, Umar ibn Abd Allah al-Raqqashi narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Harun ibn Rabab narrated to us, Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, who said: The bearers of the Throne are eight; four of them say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; praise be to You for Your forbearance after Your knowledge," and four of them say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; praise be to You for Your pardon after Your power." He said: And it is as though they are looking at the sins of the children of Adam. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir: 4/73.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And ask forgiveness for those who believed﴾, meaning they say: "Our Lord." ﴿You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾: it was said that it is in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir), and it was said it is by transposition (naql), meaning: Your mercy and Your knowledge have encompassed all things. ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾, that is, Your religion, ﴿and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire.﴾ Mutarrif said: The most sincere of Allah's servants toward the believers are the angels, and the most deceitful of creation toward the believers are the devils. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verse 8:

﴿Our Lord, admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The believer enters Paradise and says: "Where is my father? Where is my mother, where is my child, where is my spouse?" It is said: "They did not do deeds like yours." He says: "I used to work for myself and for them." So it is said: "Admit them to Paradise." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 24/45.]]

**Ma'alim al-Tanzil** (The Landmarks of Revelation) of **al-Baghawi**, on Surah 40, verses 9–11:

﴿And protect them from the evil deeds﴾, meaning the punishments. ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds﴾ means: whoever You protect from evil deeds, meaning the punishments. It was also said: the recompense of evil deeds. ﴿On that Day, You have indeed had mercy on him. That is the great triumph.﴾

The statement of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to﴾ on the Day of Resurrection while they are in the Fire, and they will loathe themselves when their evil deeds are displayed to them and they witness the punishment. It will be said to them: ﴿Certainly, the hatred of Allah toward you is greater than your hatred of yourselves, when you were being called to faith but you disbelieved.﴾ That is, the hatred of Allah toward you in the world, when you were being called to faith and you disbelieved, is greater than your hatred of yourselves today, when the punishment has descended upon you.

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice."﴾ Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, along with Qatadah and al-Dahhak, said: They were dead in the loins of their fathers, then Allah gave them life in the world, then He caused them to die the death that is unavoidable, then He gave them life for the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection. So these are two deaths and two lives.[[Al-Suyuti mentioned it in ad-Durr al-Manthur: 7/278, attributing it to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] This is like His statement, exalted is He: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life again.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. Al-Suddi said: They were made to die in the world, then they were given life in their graves for questioning, then they were made to die in their graves, then they were given life in the Hereafter.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 24/48.]]

﴿So we have acknowledged our sins. Is there any way to get out?﴾ That is: is there any exit from the Fire to the world, so that we may amend our deeds and act in obedience to You? Its parallel is His statement: ﴿Is there any way to return?﴾ [al-Shura: 44].

Here there is an elided element (matruk, a word omitted because the context makes it clear), and its meaning (majaz, the intended sense) is: "So they were answered: there is no way to that. ﴿He it is who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky﴾, meaning the rain, which is the cause of provision. ﴿And none takes heed﴾, none is admonished by these signs, ﴿except he who turns back﴾, who returns to Allah, the Exalted, in all his affairs.

﴿So call upon Allah, making the religion sincerely His﴾, meaning obedience and worship.

﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it﴾.

﴿Exalted in degrees﴾, raising the ranks of the prophets and the friends of Allah in Paradise. ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾, its Creator and Owner. ﴿He casts the Spirit﴾, He sends down the revelation, and it is called a spirit because hearts are given life by it, just as bodies are given life by spirits. ﴿Of His command﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "of His decree." It was also said: "of His word." Muqatil said: "by His command."

﴿Upon whomever of His servants He wills, that he may warn﴾, that is, that the Prophet may warn by the revelation, ﴿of the Day of Meeting﴾. Yaʿqub read it with the letter ta', meaning: "that you, O Muhammad, may warn of the Day of Meeting," the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet. Qatadah and Muqatil said: "On it the creation and the Creator meet." Ibn Zayd said: "The servants meet one another." Maymun ibn Mihran said: "The oppressor and the oppressed meet, and the adversaries." It was also said: "The worshippers and those worshipped meet." It was also said: "A person meets his deeds on it." [[Al-Qurtubi mentions these opinions: 15/300.]]

﴿The Day when they will come forth﴾, emerging from their graves, visible, with nothing concealing them, ﴿and nothing of them will be hidden from Allah﴾, of their deeds and states, ﴿anything﴾. Allah, the Exalted, says on that Day, after the creation has perished: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion today?﴾

So no one answers Him, and He answers Himself, saying: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾, who subdued the creation by death.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verse 17–21:

﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ He recompenses the good-doer for his good deeds, and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing.

﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day.﴾ That is, the Day of Resurrection. It is called that because it is near, since everything that is coming is near. Its parallel is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The Approaching Day has drawn near﴾ [al-Najm: 57], meaning the Resurrection has drawn near. ﴿When hearts will rise up to the throats, choking with grief.﴾ That is because hearts will leave their places out of fear until they reach the throats, so they neither return to their places nor leave their mouths so that they might die and find rest. ﴿Choking﴾ means distressed, filled with fear and sorrow. Al-kazm (suppression) is the repeated restraint of rage, fear, and grief within the heart until it constricts.

﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾ That is, no close friend who will benefit them, ﴿nor any intercessor who will be obeyed﴾, so that he might intercede for them.

﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾, that is, their treachery, which is the furtive glance at what is not lawful. Mujahid said: it is the gaze of the eyes at what Allah has forbidden.

﴿And what the breasts conceal.﴾

﴿Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him judge nothing.﴾ [That is, the idols.] ﴿They judge nothing﴾ because they know nothing and have no power over anything. Nafi' [and Ibn 'Amir] recited "tad'una" with a ta' (you invoke), while the others recited it with a ya' (they invoke).

﴿Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "minkum" with a kaf (you), and so it is in their codices. ﴿And in traces upon the earth﴾, but that did not benefit them. ﴿So Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah﴾, one who would repel the punishment from them.

ذَلِكَ (That) means: that punishment which befell them, "because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment."

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: "And We certainly sent Musa (Moses) with Our signs and a clear authority, to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and Haman and Qarun (Korah), but they said, 'A sorcerer, a liar.' Then when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who believe with him,'" meaning Fir'awn and his people. Qatadah said: "This was other than the first killing, because Fir'awn had stopped killing the boys, and when Musa, peace be upon him, was sent, he renewed the killing against them. So its meaning is: renew the killing against them." [[Cited by al-Qurtubi: 15/305.]] "And spare their women," so that by this they would turn them away from following Musa and supporting him. "And the plotting of the disbelievers is only in error," meaning the scheming and deception of Fir'awn and his people; their plotting goes in vain, and what Allah the Mighty and Majestic wills comes upon them.

"And Fir'awn said" to his chiefs, "Leave me to kill Musa, and let him call upon his Lord." He said this only because among the close circle of Fir'awn's people there were those who would prevent him from killing Musa, out of fear of the consequences. "Let him call upon his Lord," meaning: let Musa call upon his Lord, whom he claims sent him to us, so that He may protect him from us. "Indeed I fear that he will change" (yubaddila), meaning alter, "your religion" which you follow, "or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land." Ya'qub and the people of Kufa read "aw an yazhara" (with a fatha on the ya' and ha'), and the others read "wa an yazhara." The people of Madinah, Basrah and Hafs read "yuzhira" (with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the ha', in the causative form). "Al-fasad" (corruption) is in the accusative because it follows "an yubaddila dinakum," so that both verbs share one pattern. The others read with a fatha on the ya' and ha' (intransitive), and "al-fasad" is in the nominative. By "corruption" they mean changing the religion and worshipping other than him.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verses 27–28:**

﴿And Moses said﴾ when Pharaoh threatened him with killing, ﴿"I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning." And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said﴾.

They differed about this believer. Muqatil and al-Suddi said: he was a Copt, a cousin of Pharaoh, and he is the one whom Allah described when He said: "And a man came running from the farthest part of the city" (28:20). Others said he was an Israelite. The meaning of the verse is: "And a believing man who concealed his faith from the family of Pharaoh said." According to Ibn Abbas and most scholars, his name was Hizqil. Ibn Ishaq said his name was [Jubran] [[In manuscript "B" it is Jibril.]]. It was also said that the name of the man from the family of Pharaoh who believed was Habib [[This last opinion is mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/285). Al-Tabari (24/58) mentions the two previous opinions and, giving preference, says: "The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the one stated by al-Suddi, that the believing man was from the family of Pharaoh, since he gave heed to their speech, listened to what Moses said, and held back from killing Moses when he forbade it, and he said to them what he said: 'I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct.' If he had been an Israelite, it would have been more likely that this speaker would be punished immediately for his words to him and to his chiefs, because they did not consult the Israelites, considering them enemies. How then would it be regarding his statement about killing Moses, had he found a way to him? But since he was of the chiefs of his people, they listened to his words and refrained from what they had intended against Moses." End of quotation.]].

﴿"Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah'?"﴾, that is, because he says, "My Lord is Allah". ﴿"And he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord,"﴾ that is, signs that indicate his truthfulness. ﴿"And if he is a liar, then his lie is upon him"﴾ [[That is, will this not harm you?]]. ﴿"And if he is truthful"﴾ and you deny him, ﴿"some of what he threatens you with will befall you."﴾ Abu Ubayd said: by "some" is meant "all", meaning: if you kill him while he is truthful, what he threatens you with of punishment will befall you. Al-Laith said: "some" is redundant (ṣila), meaning: "what he threatens you with will befall you." The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: this is according to the apparent sense in argumentation, as if he said: "At the least, if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you, and in some of that is your destruction." So he mentioned "some" in order to imply "all". ﴿"Indeed, Allah does not guide to His religion"﴾ ﴿"one who is a transgressor"﴾ [[Mushrik (polytheist), an addition from "B".]] ﴿"a liar"﴾ against Allah.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi narrated to me, saying: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: I said to Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As: "Tell me of the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was praying in the courtyard of the Ka'bah, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came, seized the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), twisted his garment around his neck, and choked him with it, a severe choking. Then Abu Bakr came, seized Uqbah's shoulder, pushed him away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: 'Will you kill a man because he says, "My Lord is Allah", and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, Surah al-Mu'min: 8/553–554.]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil, "Landmarks of the Revelation") on Surah 40, verses 29–32:**

﴿O my people, the dominion is yours today, dominant in the land﴾: victorious in the land of Egypt. ﴿So who will help us against the might of Allah﴾: who will protect us from the punishment of Allah. ﴿If it comes to us﴾. The meaning is: the dominion is yours today, so do not expose yourselves to the punishment of Allah by denying Him and by killing the Prophet, for there is no one to prevent the punishment of Allah if it descends upon you. ﴿Fir'awn said: I only show you﴾ of opinion and advice, ﴿what I see﴾ for myself. Al-Dahhak said: "I only inform you of what I know." ﴿And I guide you only to the path of right guidance﴾: I only call you to the way of guidance.

﴿And the one who believed said: O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions, like the custom of the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them﴾: that is, like their habit of persisting in denial until the punishment came upon them. ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice to the servants﴾: that is, He does not destroy them before the proof has been established against them.

﴿And O my people, I fear for you the day of calling out﴾: the Day of Resurrection, when every people will be called with their leader, and some will call out to others. The companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire, and the companions of the Fire to the companions of the Garden. The people of the Heights will be called, and it will be announced concerning happiness and misery: "Verily, so-and-so son of so-and-so has been granted a happiness after which he will never be wretched again, and so-and-so son of so-and-so has been made wretched with a wretchedness after which he will never be happy again." And at the time when death is slaughtered it will be called out: "O people of the Garden, eternity, there is no death! And O people of the Fire, eternity, there is no death!"

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak recited "yawm al-tanad" (يَوْمَ التَّنَادِّ) with a doubled dal, meaning the day of mutual aversion (al-tanafur). That is because they will flee and scatter across the earth, as camels scatter when they bolt away from their owners.

Al-Dahhak said: Likewise, when they hear the roaring of the Fire, they will flee in scattering. They will not reach any region of the regions except that they will find the angels in ranks, so they will return to the place where they were. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the angel will be upon its edges﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 17]. And His saying: "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except by authority." Then Allah informed about their abode on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour arises: "Enter, O people of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment."﴾ Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr and Abu Bakr recited "al-sa'ah" and "udkhulu" (the Arabic forms) with the alif of the hamzat al-wasl (connecting hamza) omitted in connection, and with its vowel (damma) at the beginning, and with the kha' vowelled with damma from the verb "dukhul" (entering). Meaning: It is said to them: "Enter, O people of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment." Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 40, verses 47–50:

﴿And when they dispute with one another in the Fire﴾. That is: O Muhammad, mention to your people when they argue, meaning the people of the Fire, within the Fire. ﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers (*tabaʿ*)﴾ in the world, ﴿so will you avail us any portion of the Fire?"﴾ The word *tabaʿ* (followers) is used both as singular and plural according to the people of Basrah. Its singular is *tabiʿ*. The people of Kufah said: it is a plural with no singular, and its plural is *atbaʿ*.

﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants."﴾ And those in the Fire will say, when the punishment has become severe upon them, ﴿to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error.﴾

That is: it is futile, leads astray, and does not benefit them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verses 51–56:

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By victory and dominance." Al-Dahhak said: "By proof, and in the Hereafter by excuse." It was also said: "By taking revenge on the enemies in this world and the Hereafter." All of these were granted to the prophets and the believers. They are helped with proof against those who oppose them, and Allah has helped them with dominance over those who opposed them and with the destruction of their enemies. He also helped them after they were killed, by taking revenge on their enemies, as He helped Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah): when he was killed, seventy thousand were killed in retribution for him. So they are helped in one of these ways. ﴿And on the day when the witnesses will stand﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, the guardian angels will stand and bear witness for the messengers that they delivered the message, and against the disbelievers that they denied it.

﴿On the day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾: if they make excuses for their disbelief, they will not be accepted; and if they repent, it will not benefit them. ﴿And for them is the curse﴾: distance from mercy. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning Hell.

﴿And We certainly gave Musa (Moses) the guidance﴾. Muqatil said: "The guidance from misguidance, meaning the Torah." ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ [the Torah] [[Addition from manuscript "b".]].

﴿A guidance and a reminder for those of understanding﴾.

﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, over their harm. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾ regarding the manifestation of your religion and the destruction of your enemies ﴿is true﴾. Al-Kalbi said: "The verse of fighting abrogated (naskh, meaning the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) the verse of patience" [See what has preceded: 3/32, note (1)]. ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. This is an act of worship commanded by Allah, so that He may raise him by it in rank, and so that it becomes a sunnah (established practice) for those after him. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray while thanking your Lord, ﴿in the evening and the morning﴾. Al-Hasan said: "It means the 'Asr prayer and the Fajr prayer." Ibn 'Abbas said: "The five prayers."

﴿Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts﴾ except what is in their hearts; the chest is the place of the heart, so it is used to refer to the heart because of their close proximity. ﴿But pride﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "What drives them to deny you is nothing but the pride and greatness in their breasts." ﴿They will never attain it﴾. Mujahid said: "They will never attain the object of that pride, because Allah the Mighty and Majestic will humiliate them."

Ibn Qutaybah said: "There is nothing in their breasts except arrogance toward Muhammad ﷺ and greed to overcome him" [In Gharib al-Qur'an: "(that they kill you)"; see al-Qurtayn by Ibn Mutarrif: 2/106.] "and they will never attain that."

The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, because they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Our companion, al-Masih ibn Dawud" (they mean the Dajjal, the Antichrist), "will come out at the end of time, and his authority will reach across land and sea, and he will return the kingdom to us" [See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/294.]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ from the trial of the Dajjal. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: "The verse of fighting abrogated (naskh, meaning the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) the verse of patience" [See what has preceded: 3/32, note (1)]. ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. This is an act of worship commanded by Allah, so that He may raise him by it in rank, and so that it becomes a sunnah (established practice) for those after him. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray while thanking your Lord, ﴿in the evening and the morning﴾. Al-Hasan said: "It means the 'Asr prayer and the Fajr prayer." Ibn 'Abbas said: "The five prayers."

﴿Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts﴾ except what is in their hearts; the chest is the place of the heart, so it is used to refer to the heart because of their close proximity. ﴿But pride﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "What drives them to deny you is nothing but the pride and greatness in their breasts." ﴿They will never attain it﴾. Mujahid said: "They will never attain the object of that pride, because Allah the Mighty and Majestic will humiliate them."

Ibn Qutaybah said: "There is nothing in their breasts except arrogance toward Muhammad ﷺ and greed to overcome him" [In Gharib al-Qur'an: "(that they kill you)"; see al-Qurtayn by Ibn Mutarrif: 2/106.] "and they will never attain that."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ from the trial of the Dajjal. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verse 57:**

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, despite their greatness, ﴿is greater﴾, meaning greater in hearts, ﴿than the creation of mankind﴾, meaning than their resurrection after death. ﴿But most people﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿do not know﴾, in that they do not draw from it evidence for the oneness of its Creator. Some people said: "Greater" [meaning: more important] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] than the creation of the Dajjal (the false messiah, Antichrist). ﴿But most people do not know﴾, meaning the Jews, who dispute concerning the matter of the Dajjal.

It is narrated from Hisham ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Since the creation of Adam until the Hour is established, there has been no creation greater than the creation of the Dajjal" [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Fitan, chapter: On the remaining hadiths about the Dajjal, no. (2946): 4/2266-2267.]].

Abu Sa'id Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us, saying: my grandfather Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us, [Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari informed us, Abd al-Razzaq] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] informed us: Ma'mar related to us from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid al-Ansariyyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house when he mentioned the Dajjal, and he said: "Before him there will be three years. In the first year, the sky will withhold a third of its rain and the earth a third of its vegetation. In the second year, the sky will withhold two-thirds of its rain and the earth two-thirds of its vegetation. In the third year, the sky will withhold all its rain and the earth all its vegetation, so that no animal with hooves or with molars will remain except that it perishes. Among the most severe of his trials is that he will come to a Bedouin and say: 'Tell me, if I bring your camels back to life, will you not know that I am your Lord?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then there will appear to him the likeness of his camels, with the most beautiful udders and the largest humps. And he will come to a man whose brother and father have died and say: 'Tell me, if I bring your father and your brother back to life, will you not know that I am your Lord?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then Satan will appear to him in the likeness of his father and his brother."

She said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out for his need, and then returned while the people were in concern and grief over what he had told them. She said: He took hold of the two sides of the door and said: "Mahyam, Asma'?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have struck our hearts with the mention of the Dajjal." He said: "If he comes out while I am alive, then I will be his opponent (hajij); and if not, then indeed my Lord is my successor over every believer." Asma' said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, we knead dough and do not bake it until we are hungry, so how will the believers be on that day?" He said: "What suffices the people of heaven of glorification and sanctification will suffice them" [[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, 11/391, and from his chain by Imam Ahmad: 6/453. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/344-345 and said: "All of it was narrated by Ahmad and al-Tabarani through several chains; in one of them: before his emergence there will be five years of drought. It contains Shahr ibn Hawshab, in whom there is weakness, but he has been declared trustworthy." The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/60-61.]].

With this same chain he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Dajjal will remain on earth for forty years: a year like a month, a month like a week, a week like a day, and a day like the flaring of a palm frond in fire" [[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 11/392, and from his chain by Imam Ahmad: 6/454. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/347, attributing it to al-Tabarani, and criticized it on account of Shahr, saying: "Its contradiction of the authentic hadiths cannot be admitted: that he remains on earth forty days, and in this [narration] forty years." The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/62.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Tahiri informed us, my grandfather Abd al-Samad al-Bazzar informed us, Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us, Ishaq al-Dabari informed us, Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among the people, praised Allah with what is due to Him, then mentioned the Dajjal and said: "Indeed I warn you about him, and there was no prophet except that he warned his people. Noah warned his people, but I will say to you about him a saying that no prophet has said to his people: you know that he is one-eyed, and that Allah is not one-eyed" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter: the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And We certainly sent Noah to his people" 6/370. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/49.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Musa ibn Isma'il informed us, Juwayriyah related to us from Nafi', from Abd Allah, who said: The Dajjal was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed Allah is not hidden from you. Indeed Allah is not one-eyed," and he pointed with his hand to his eye, "and indeed the Masih al-Dajjal is one-eyed in the right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter: the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "and that you may be brought up under My eye" 13/389.]].

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Ali ibn Hujr informed us, Shu'ayb ibn Safwan informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ribi ibn Hirash, from Uqbah ibn Amr ibn Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: I went with him to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Uqbah said to him: "Tell me what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the Dajjal." He said: "Indeed the Dajjal will emerge, and with him is water and fire. As for what people see as water, it is a burning fire; and as for what people see as fire, it is cold, sweet water. So whoever among you encounters that, let him fall into what he sees as fire, for indeed it is sweet, good water." Uqbah said: "I too have heard it," confirming Hudhayfah [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Fitan, chapter on mentioning the Dajjal, his description and those with him, no. (2934/2935) 4/2250. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/52.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to me, Ibn al-Walid related to us, Ibn Amr, who is al-Awza'i, related to us, Ishaq related to us, Anas ibn Malik related to me, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no town except that the Dajjal will tread upon it, except Makkah and Madinah. (2943): 4/2265. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/326.]].

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Tayswafuni informed us, Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari informed us, Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihayni related to us, Ali ibn Hujr related to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far related to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Masih will come from the direction of the east, his aim being Madinah, until he descends at the back of Uhud. Then the angels will turn his face toward Syria, and there he will perish" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter on protecting Madinah from the entry of plague and the Dajjal, no. (1380) 2/1005. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/326.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Tahiri informed us, my grandfather Abd al-Samad al-Bazzar informed us, Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us, Ishaq al-Dabari informed us, Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand of my ummah will follow the Dajjal, wearing green shawls (al-sijan, i.e., green tayalisan)" [[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (Kitab al-Jami'): 11/393. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/62, and in its chain is Abu Harun al-Abdi, who is abandoned (matruk).]]. And Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrates it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "On that day, with the Dajjal will be seventy thousand Jews, all of them possessing a crown and a sword adorned with ornament" [[A portion of a long hadith narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, chapter: the trial of the Dajjal, no. (4077) 2/1359-1363. Al-Hakim also narrated it in abridged form and declared it sahih according to the conditions of Muslim: 4/536-537. Al-Suyuti attributes it in Kanz al-Ummal: 14/296 to Ibn Khuzaymah and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verses 58–60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.﴾ The people of Kufa read "tatadhakkarun" (you remember) with the taa' (second person), while the others read it with the yaa' (third person), because the beginning and the end of the verses are a report about a people.

﴿Indeed, the Hour﴾, that is, the Resurrection, ﴿is surely coming, there is no doubt in it, but most of the people do not believe.﴾

﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you.﴾ That is: worship Me alone, and I will answer you, reward you, and forgive you. Since He expressed worship by supplication (du'a'), He made turning in devotion (inabah) a form of responding.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani narrated to us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us from Mansur, from Abu Dharr, from Yusay' al-Kindi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say from the pulpit: "Indeed, supplication is worship," then he recited: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salah, Bab al-Du'a': 2/141; al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, Tafsir Surat al-Mu'min: 9/121-122, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir: 2/253; Ibn Majah in al-Du'a', Bab Fadl al-Du'a', no. (3828): 2/1258; Ibn Hibban in al-Adiyah, Bab ma ja'a fi fadl al-du'a', no. (2396), p. 595; al-Hakim: 1/490, who authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed; al-Tayalisi: 1/153; al-Tabari: 24/79; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/184.]]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Dawraqi informed us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Shirazi narrated to us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qurashi informed us in Baghdad, Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn al-Ala' narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Budayl narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Abu al-Malih narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Salih mention from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, Allah becomes angry with him." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat: 9/313; Ibn Majah in al-Du'a', Bab Fadl al-Du'a', no. (3827): 2/1258; Imam Ahmad: 2/442; al-Hakim: 1/491; al-Tabari: 24/79; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/188. Abu Salih al-Khuzi: Ibn Ma'in declared him weak. See Fath al-Bari: 11/95.]]

It is also said: supplication is remembrance (dhikr) and asking (su'al). ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far and Abu Bakr read "yudkhalun" (they will be made to enter) with a dammah on the yaa' and a fathah on the khaa', while the others read it with a fathah on the yaa' and a dammah on the khaa'. "Dakhirin" means lowly and humiliated.

﴿Say: "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides God, since the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ This was when he was called to disbelief.

﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 40, verses 81–85:**

﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, meaning the proofs of His power. ﴿So which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in number, mightier in strength and in monuments upon the earth﴾, meaning their factories (maṣāniʿ) and their palaces (quṣūr). ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾, meaning it did not benefit them. It has also been said that this is in the sense of a question, and its implied meaning is: "What did their earnings avail them?"

﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced﴾, meaning they were pleased ﴿with what knowledge they had.﴾ Mujahid said: it is their saying, "We are more knowledgeable; we will not be resurrected and we will not be punished." He called that "knowledge" according to what they claimed and asserted, while in reality it is ignorance.

﴿And there befell them what they used to mock. Then when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾, meaning: we disavow what we used to set up as equal to Allah.

﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our might﴾, meaning Our punishment. ﴿[This is] the way of Allah which has already passed among His servants﴾. It has been said that the word ﴿sunnata﴾ (way/practice) is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, meaning "like the way of Allah." It has also been said that it is an infinitive (maṣdar). And it has been said that it is in the sense of a warning, meaning: "Beware of the way of Allah." ﴿That is the way of Allah which has passed among His servants﴾, and that way is that when they witness Allah's punishment they believe, but their faith does not benefit them at the witnessing of the punishment.

﴿And the disbelievers were lost there﴾, by the loss of both abodes. Al-Zajjaj said: the disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss becomes evident to them when they see the punishment.
